paper_metadata.title: Extracting a function encoded in amplitudes of a quantum state by tensor network and orthogonal function expansion

summary: The paper proposes a gate-based quantum method to read out functions encoded in amplitudes using orthogonal-function expansion combined with a matrix product state (MPS) approximation. A classical numerical experiment on a 5‑asset worst‑of put option (D = r = 16) shows that an MPS representation with 12,544 parameters approximates the function with maximum error ≈0.51 relative to Monte Carlo while compressing the full cosine coefficient tensor (≈1,048,576 parameters) by two orders of magnitude. Additional experiments show power‑law error decay with increasing degrees of freedom.

experiments.description: Classical numerical experiment demonstrating the proposed gate-based quantum readout method by optimizing an MPS-encoded approximation of a five-asset worst-of put option price using cosine orthogonal functions; the quantum circuit is described as applicable to gate-based QC, but the reported experiment itself is performed classically with the quantum circuit absorbed into tensor calculations.

algorithm.variant: Tensor-network-encoded orthogonal-function readout via alternating optimization of MPS blocks
algorithm.ansatz: Matrix product state (MPS) circuit encoding of coefficient tensor
algorithm.optimizer: Alternating optimization via SVD updates of block unitaries

hyperparameters.grid_points: minimal grid points with ngr = D in the classical experiment

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial values of the unitaries V^1,...,V^{d-1} may be chosen randomly

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Function values are expanded in tensorized cosine basis; coefficients are approximated by an MPS and encoded into a quantum state in the proposed method
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize fidelity F = <f|f~> between the target function-encoding state and the MPS-based approximation state
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints beyond right-canonical MPS structure and unitary block updates

problem_instance.description: Five-asset worst-of put option pricing under the Black-Scholes model

dataset_specification.description: Underlying assets priced under BS model; parameters r_RF = 0, sigma_i = 0.2 for i=1..5, K = 100, T = 1; random sample points drawn from the distribution of S(t) at t=1 with initial value (K,...,K)

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Grid values of the target function computed by Monte Carlo integration with 10^5 sample paths; cosine basis used on hyperrectangle [L_i,U_i] with L_i = 0.01K and U_i set by Eq. (C6)
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Accuracy evaluated on the diagonal line s1=...=sd and on 10^4 random sample points; compared against Monte Carlo values and full cosine expansion

hardware.framework: ITensor (classical tensor-network library used for the numerical experiment)

implementation_details.classical_solver: ITensor-based tensor calculations; Monte Carlo integration for target values
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute target function values on grid points via Monte Carlo integration; calculate cosine-expansion coefficients; use minimal grid ngr = D for the classical experiment
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Construct MPS-based approximation and compare against Monte Carlo and full cosine expansion

speedup_claims.factor: exponential reduction in readout bottleneck avoided; polynomial evaluation O(dr^2D + rD^2) instead of O(D^d)
speedup_claims.baseline_method: full tensorized orthogonal expansion / naive coefficient handling
speedup_claims.conditions: when the coefficient tensor is approximated by an MPS and evaluated classically from the compressed representation
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a complexity claim for the approximation/evaluation scheme, not a hardware-demonstrated runtime speedup. The numerical experiment was performed classically.

speedup_claims.factor: avoids exponential dependence on d in coefficient extraction in principle
speedup_claims.baseline_method: direct amplitude readout or full tensorized orthogonal expansion
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming access to the proposed gate-based oracle and quantum circuit construction
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not provide a total query complexity bound or a demonstrated end-to-end quantum speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(dr^2D + rD^2) for evaluating the MPS-based approximation; proposed readout method aims to avoid exponential dependence on d in coefficient extraction
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(D^d) for full tensorized orthogonal expansion without MPS compression

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Requires access to an oracle O_f preparing |f⟩ and additional orthogonal-function state-preparation oracles V_OF^i; concrete qubit counts, depths, and logical resource estimates are not provided.
limiting_factors: No implementation on a quantum device
No total query-complexity bound for the readout procedure
Requires oracle preparation of |f⟩ and orthogonal-function states
Accuracy demonstrated only for a 5-dimensional finance function

notes: The paper presents a gate-based quantum circuit construction, but the only numerical experiment is performed classically; no actual QPU, qubit count, or circuit depth for a hardware run is reported.
num_variational_params inferred from the reported MPS DOF in the experiment: 12544.
hardware.type set to not_specified because the experiment uses classical tensor calculations rather than a quantum device.
The paper proposes a gate-based readout method but performs only classical numerical experiments; no quantum runtime comparison or empirical speedup is shown.
Speedup claims are complexity-theoretic and conditional on oracle availability.

experiments.description: Additional numerical experiment studying the relationship between approximation accuracy and degrees of freedom using an alternative quantum-circuit ansatz V'_MPS with sliding m_bl‑qubit blocks (Fig. 5), comparing error scaling versus DOF against truncated cosine expansions.

algorithm.variant: Sliding-block tensor-network circuit V'_MPS for coefficient encoding
algorithm.ansatz: Parameterized circuit with overlapping m_bl-qubit blocks replacing the standard MPS circuit
algorithm.optimizer: Alternating block optimization maximizing ⟨a|ã′⟩ similar to Algorithm 1

key_results: Approximation error versus degrees of freedom exhibits a power-law decay in the high-DOF regime (Fig. 6).
For comparable DOF, the tensor-network circuit approximation achieves significantly lower error than low-degree cosine expansions.
Scaling behavior similar to finite-entanglement scaling in tensor-network studies.
